text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Bank unions vow to fight government plans to reform a 1937 decree setting strict limits for branch opening hours, which is to be examined in cabinet today.
-- French government asks for more time from European Commission, to widen state plan to restructure textile sector.
-- CGT union to block newspapers from being published on Thursday.

-- Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet to be chief executive of new company to be created by a planned merger between Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux, which is expected to be approved by the two companies' boards on Friday.
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot to announce further cuts in labour charges today, as a result of an expected rejection by EU authorities of French state help to the textile sector.
-- Air Liberte and TAT chairman Marc Rochet says in an interview he expects the group to reach breakeven within two years. Cockpit crew unions to strike today.
-- Negotiations to resume tomorrow at World Trade Organisation in Geneva toward an international agreement on financial services.
-- Employment outlook remains gloomy for executives, as firms are seen creating less executive jobs in 1997 than in 1996.
-- EDF utility and Nuclear Energy Council opposed on evaluation of nuclear waste treatment and disposal by Cogema.
-- Government seeks to extend business hours for banks.
